headline: Sensex and Nifty Gain on Banking and FMCG Support Amid Global Selloff and US Market Crash

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: FII buying activity and strong support from the banking and FMCG sectors drove the domestic market rally.
The Sensex gained 512 points to close at 25,291, while the Nifty approached the 25,300 mark.
Strong domestic buying helped the market overcome a deepening selloff in global and Asian stocks.
Specific stock recommendations and buy calls from analysts boosted investor confidence in select counters.
whatHappening: The Indian government increased export duties on diesel to ₹2.5/litre and ATF to ₹1.5/litre.
Shares of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) reached an all-time high, with market capitalization exceeding ₹5 trillion.
Cyclone Akvan is intensifying over the Bay of Bengal, putting the coasts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on high alert.
Data indicates that 6 out of 10 NSE-listed stocks are still trading below their closing levels from December 2025.
summary: Indian indices Sensex and Nifty gained over 0.5% led by banking and FMCG sectors, despite a significant global selloff. Investors are reacting to a hike in fuel export duties and weak cues from Wall Street ahead of Nvidia's earnings. Domestic focus also remains on the intensifying Cyclone Akvan and specific stock recommendations from market analysts.
